headline: BARNAT PIT SUSPENDED AFTER WALL MOVEMENT — AGNICO EAGLE FLAGS 60,000–80,000 OZ H2 PRODUCTION HIT AT CANADIAN MALARTIC (TSX:AEM)
snippet: A rock mass movement on July 1, 2026 along the north wall of the Barnat open pit at Agnico Eagle's Canadian Malartic Complex in Québec triggered an immediate suspension of in-pit mining operations — announced July 2, 2026. No injuries, equipment damage, or environmental impact resulted. The affected area had been previously identified as containing weaker geological structures and was subject to enhanced geotechnical monitoring; technical teams are now conducting a detailed stability assessment before determining the path forward. During the suspension, the processing plant will draw from low-grade ore stockpiles. Agnico Eagle now expects the incident to reduce H2 2026 production at Canadian Malartic by approximately 60,000 to 80,000 ounces of gold. At spot gold near $4,183/oz, a 70,000-oz midpoint reduction represents roughly $293 million in foregone revenue — a material impact for investors and royalty holders (OR Royalties holds a 1.5% NSR on portions of the Malartic complex). Canadian Malartic is Agnico Eagle's largest single producing asset; this is the most significant operational disruption at the mine in several years and warrants close monitoring as the geotechnical assessment progresses.

headline: $1.4B NPV, 46.5% IRR — KWYJIBO RARE EARTH PEA DELIVERS DYSPROSIUM-RICH ECONOMICS IN QUÉBEC WITH A 2.67-HECTARE SURFACE FOOTPRINT (CSE:CLM)
snippet: Consolidated Lithium Metals Inc. (CSE:CLM) — primarily a rare earth oxide developer despite its name — released an Updated Preliminary Economic Assessment on July 2, 2026 for the 100%-optioned Kwyjibo REO Project in Québec's Côte-Nord region, returning a post-tax NPV of CA$1.4 billion (US$987M) at a 7% discount rate, a 46.5% pre-tax IRR, 35.4% post-tax IRR, two-year payback, CA$881M capex, and average annual production of 9,800 tonnes of total rare earth oxides over a 10-year underground mine life. The project's most notable design feature is a 2.67-hectare surface footprint — smaller than most sporting facilities — with all processing located offsite and no residues stored at the mine site, substantially simplifying permitting. Kwyjibo's heavy rare earth profile is enriched in dysprosium and terbium — the two most geopolitically restricted rare earths under China's export licensing regime, with approval rates for dysprosium compounds falling below 15% for some Western industrial buyers in Q2 2026. At 650km northeast of Québec City in Côte-Nord, the project is within a Québec jurisdiction that has proactively streamlined critical mineral permitting since 2024. CLM holds an option to earn an 80% undivided interest from SOQUEM Inc. by solely funding exploration expenditures.

headline: SECTION 232 FINALIZED: 15% US COPPER TARIFF STARTS JAN 2027, RISING TO 30% IN 2028 — COMEX INVENTORIES HIT RECORD 650,000 TONNES AS BUYERS FRONT-RUN
snippet: The U.S. Commerce Department's Section 232 copper review concluded June 30, 2026 with a recommended tariff structure now before the President for a formal determination: a 15% tariff on refined copper imports beginning January 2027, potentially escalating to 30% from 2028 onward. COMEX copper warehouse inventories surged to a record 650,000 tonnes as domestic buyers aggressively front-ran the implementation window. Goldman Sachs flagged that once the tariff structure is formally enacted, copper could breach US$14,000/tonne (~$6.35/lb) on tariff-driven inventory dynamics alone. Copper futures traded near $6.17–$6.20/lb in early July, supported by both the rate-hike repricing after the June payrolls miss and the tariff-driven domestic production premium. For junior mining investors, the Section 232 finalization crystallises the long-term case for North American copper projects — particularly those in U.S. jurisdictions (Idaho, Arizona, Nevada, Minnesota, Wyoming) and Canada — as tariff-adjacent domestic supply now commands an explicit and widening premium in offtake negotiations and private placement financing. Chile's May copper output fell nearly 13% year-on-year, amplifying the supply signal.

headline: CHINA LITHIUM FUTURES +6% TO 165,250 CNY/T, UP 165% YEAR-ON-YEAR — PLS NGUNGAJU RESTART BEGINS AS CATL MINE SHUTDOWN AND ZIMBABWE BAN SQUEEZE SUPPLY
snippet: China lithium carbonate futures surged approximately 6% to 165,250 CNY/T (approximately US$22,800/tonne), 165% above year-ago levels, as three converging supply shocks hit simultaneously in late June and early July 2026: CATL suspended operations at its Jianxiawo lepidolite mine in Jiangxi province (one of China's largest sources); Zimbabwe's export ban on lithium concentrate removed an estimated 9–10% of 2026 projected global supply; and China's regulatory crackdown revoked 27 Jiangxi mining permits. ASX lithium producers Pilbara Minerals (ASX:PLS), Liontown Resources (ASX:LTR), and Mineral Resources (ASX:MIN) posted material gains. Pilbara's Ngungaju plant — a ~200,000-tonne-per-annum processing facility at its Pilgangoora operation — approved for restart as of early July 2026 with ramp-up through the September quarter, adds meaningful production leverage precisely as the structural squeeze intensifies. Battery energy storage system demand, driven by China's grid infrastructure mandates, has become an independent demand driver alongside EVs; analysts note the current rally is more fundamentally grounded than the 2022–2023 speculative bubble.

headline: GENERATION URANIUM BOOTS ON GROUND AT ANGILAK — INAUGURAL SUMMER FIELD PROGRAM BEGINS AT YATH PROJECT IN NUNAVUT'S KIVALLIQ URANIUM CAMP (TSXV:GEN)
snippet: Generation Uranium Inc. (TSXV:GEN) mobilized its summer 2026 field crew to the Yath Project in Nunavut's Kivalliq Region on July 2, 2026, commencing its inaugural surface exploration program in the Angilak uranium district. The team — assembled with specialists in geophysics, structural geology, and prospecting — will ground-truth historic uranium showings, refine anomalies from Expert Geophysics' Moving Loop TEM survey, and deliver a ranked drill target list ahead of the company's drill permit application. The Angilak district sits within the broader Kivalliq corridor alongside Denison Mines and Forum Energy Technologies assets, and hosted Kivalliq Energy's Lac Cinquante deposit before its acquisition. Uranium spot prices stabilized at US$84–87/lb in Q2 2026 after the January $101/lb peak; the structural long-term utility contracting deficit continues to draw exploration capital toward pre-drill stage projects in Canada's highest-grade uranium jurisdictions. Yath is among the district's largest and least-explored tenement blocks, making this inaugural ground program a genuine early-stage risk event for investors in GEN.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM DRILLS LUCKY CLIFF — PHASE II STARTS AT COPPER MOUNTAIN WYOMING WITH 4,500m PROGRAM TESTING 1970s UNION PACIFIC ANOMALY (CSE:M)
snippet: Myriad Uranium Corp. (CSE:M / OTCQB) confirmed July 2, 2026 that Phase II drilling has commenced at its Copper Mountain Uranium Project in Wyoming, targeting 4,500 metres across two stages with a potential third stage expanding the total program to 7,000–10,000 metres. The first four holes test Lucky Cliff, a high-priority target drilled by Union Pacific in the late 1970s and never followed up with modern techniques or downhole geophysics — sitting within the same structural trend as Phase I's most encouraging intercepts. Myriad holds a 75% interest in Copper Mountain with a definitive agreement to acquire the remaining 25% via its planned acquisition of Rush Rare Metals Corp. Wyoming operates under the most uranium-friendly regulatory framework in the United States, hosts the majority of U.S. conventional uranium production history, and continues to attract active drill programs in 2026 as domestic uranium supply policy becomes a priority under the Trump administration's critical minerals executive orders. Phase II assay results will determine whether the project advances to a resource estimate.

headline: GOLD +2% SILVER +7% FOR THE WEEK — METALS POST FIRST WEEKLY WIN IN FIVE WEEKS AS THIN HOLIDAY TAPE EXTENDS NFP-DRIVEN DOLLAR RETREAT
snippet: Spot gold and silver held their post-NFP gains on July 3, 2026 heading into the abbreviated pre-holiday session, posting their first weekly gains in five weeks: gold up approximately 2% for the week to $4,183/oz and silver up 7% to $62.86/oz. Rate-hike bets on the September FOMC meeting fell below 50% probability as the June payrolls miss continued to reverberate. July 4 is a non-trading day for U.S. markets (COMEX, NYSE Arca), but TSX futures edged higher on the metals strength. The combination of a weaker U.S. dollar, retreating rate-hike probabilities, and metals recovering toward key technical resistance represents the most supportive macro backdrop for junior mining equities since March 2026. Analysts caution that thin holiday liquidity has amplified the gains, and the real durability test comes when full institutional participation resumes after the long weekend. For TSX-V investors, gold price and September hike probability are the two direct inputs to how exploration-stage companies are valued heading into Q3 results season.

headline: ASSAYS DUE THIS WEEK — WA GOLD STARTS DRILLING LAST REMAINING GROUND ADJACENT TO MI6'S $1.6B BULLABULLING 4.5MOZ GOLD DEPOSIT (ASX:WAU)
snippet: WA Gold Limited (ASX:WAU) commenced a 10,000-metre drilling program on tenements immediately adjacent to Minerals 260's (ASX:MI6) Bullabulling Gold Project in Western Australia's Eastern Goldfields — a 4.5-million-ounce resource that has attracted an A$1.6-billion market cap as MI6 advances toward a development decision. WAU is now the only significant independent tenement holder remaining in the Bullabulling district after MI6 consolidated surrounding ground from approximately 130km² to 1,160km² over recent years; WAU's land could host structural extensions of the same mineralizing system driving MI6's deposit. The program began with 46 aircore holes (~3,680 metres) on eight drill lines along the northern boundary of MI6's deposit, with assays from the first three diamond core holes expected in the first week of July 2026. For investors following the Bullabulling story, WAU represents a low-market-cap option on the same district thesis that drives MI6 to premium pricing — with those first assay results shaping as the primary near-term binary catalyst. Note: Next Investors is an investment-focused editorial publication and may hold positions in ASX:WAU.
